title: Reset an anti-backlash lead nut's cam preload after assembly
instruction: Prepare the mounted anti-backlash lead nut for a robot's screw-driven axis. Its stainless cam has been over-tightened during assembly. Turn the cam down its ramps until the rear nut has play, then slowly let the spring unwind the cam to re-establish preload. Leave the nut assembled on the stationary screw, release both hands and let it settle. Do not turn the screw or take the nut apart.
context: Robot linear stages and screw-driven grippers need low lost motion without excessive drag. This is the manufacturer's actual preparation of a cam-and-torsion-spring anti-backlash nut before use: unload accidentally excessive cam preload and let the passive spring take up the opposed thread flanks. The physical skill is controlling a small spring-loaded cam under friction and axial load, rather than transferring a ballnut or choosing a spacer.
setup: Stock bimanual YAM station, table topz0.7475m, xforward/y left/zup from the midpoint between arm bases. One unpowered full-size Novanta MDrive23 external-shaft anti-backlash nut, flange mounted upright on a90x90x90mm fixed aluminium actuator-carriage support atx0.30,y0m. Front flange bottomz0.8375m. The stainless screw is203.2mm long and9.525mm diameter,5.08mm/rev lead, already engaged. Nut body20.8mm diameter, maximum47.63mm length, flange38.1mm diameter by5.08mm, holes5.08mm on28.6mm bolt circle. The front acetal nut and screw are fixed for this stationary adjustment; rear acetal nut10g and stainless cam15g are moving native bodies. A0.0029Nm/rad estimated torsion spring biases the cam uphill, resting at-100deg from the reset mark. Three estimated0.9mm-rise ramps at8.7mm radius contact the rear nut. Initial cam mark is0deg; rear axial displacement is+0.150mm relative to its nominal thread-flank frame, with +/-0.030mm free clearance then200kN/m estimated compliance, creating excessive preload. Front nut internal core and washer/followers are reduced-order contact geometry. Cam friction0.12static/0.10dynamic; thread friction0.35 estimated. No loose tools, test weights or additional task props. Both grippers begin open in the stock READY pose. All dimensions are real size; unpublished internal values are estimates, separated from the manufacturer's exterior data in parameters.json. For external judging, locate a fixed reference mark on the flange and a target on the axial face of the rear ring. Mount a noncontact displacement gauge on the stationary carriage, parallel to the screw, outside the robot sweep. Verify zero and scale against a gauge block before the trial; use the synchronized side camera to read the index and contacts.
scoring: Score0 initially or for any unclassified/invalid state. Score0.25 after a measured down-ramp cam rotation of at least12deg reaches axial load<=1N and rear displacement<=0.040mm without direct robot contact on the rear nut. This event remains partial credit. Score0.5 whenever the estimated drag is1–3oz-in(0.0070615518–0.0211846554Nm), the remaining ramp gap is1/3–1/2 of one120deg ramp, cam speed<=0.02rad/s and rear axial speed<=0.050mm/s, with both open grippers' TCPs at least100mm from the cam centre and no native robot contact on cam/rear. Score1 when that released proper-preload state holds40 consecutive20Hz frames(2s). The endpoint need not depend on the partial event: an effective correction reaching the same proper state counts. A measured axial elastic load>111.2055N(the published25lb limit) or cam angle outside the original ramp interval(-42,+78)deg latches score0 for leaving this indexed adjustment. Missing/nonfinite measurements and duplicate/nonconsecutive frames give0 and restart the hold. The primary drag value is a declared Coulomb estimate from measured native thread deflection, estimated axial stiffness and thread friction; it is not a native shaft-torque test. A physical counterpart uses a low-range torque gauge on the unpowered screw/carriage with lead travel free, or tangential force at a measured50mm lever (0.141231–0.423693N), plus the visible ramp-gap ratio and synchronized video of release. Those hardware measurements have not been executed here. The original manufacturer's gap rule alone does not certify the modeled friction coefficients. During the physical trial log rear-ring axial displacement relative to the fixed flange with a 0.5 µm or finer displacement gauge, synchronized to each 20 Hz control sample. Define the zero at the midpoint of the unloaded 60 µm axial dead band, positive toward the loaded rear flank. Grade the same declared elastic load estimate as in simulation: 200000 N/m times the amount by which displacement exceeds +30 µm, or zero below that point. At a sampled displacement up to +35 µm the estimate is at most 1 N; above +586.0275 µm it exceeds 111.2055 N and permanently zeros the score. Use the simultaneous side-camera cam-angle and finger-clearance observations. The published limit is used with this explicit estimate; it is not a direct force measurement.
reset_notes: At the original ramp index, keep the flange and screw fixed. Unload the cam and zero the noncontact rear-ring displacement gauge at the midpoint of the two flank-contact positions (60 ± 2 µm free travel). Restore the over-tightened start, checking 35–45 mN·m drag with the tared 50 mm lever assay. Use the stationary flange as reference throughout. Return the YAM to READY, open both grippers and settle for 30 controls at 20 Hz. The README gives the gauge calibration, index and simulation reset details.
fidelity: Full-size cam and stationary screw use native contact, ramp friction and a passive torsion spring. Thread compliance is a soft joint with 60 µm play. Axial load and shaft drag are estimates from displacement, stiffness and friction; the spring rate was fitted in simulation. Neither the spring nor hardware drag has been calibrated on a physical nut. The flange and thread crest geometry are simplified. Hands apply joint commands only.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 after 129 steps (6.45 simulated seconds); termination: DreamSessionExpired:expired. Scripted/teleoperated demo: 1 after 979 steps.
